title: Micrometer
prompt: A labelled teaching cutaway of the page 64 mechanical micrometer measures a thin rod. Insert externally places the rod between fixed anvil and spindle. Turn advances the spindle through its precision screw until the ratchet slips at contact rather than compressing the rod indefinitely. Read highlights the sleeve scale and fractional-turn thimble scale and adds their readings consistently with the chosen screw lead and graduations. See-through exposes the frame, anvil, spindle, fixed threaded sleeve, thimble and ratchet coupling. Do not add a digital sensor or claim numerical accuracy beyond the scale and geometry shown.
blurb: A teaching cutaway uses an enlarged 0.5 mm screw lead and 50 thimble divisions to measure a rigid rod, with a simplified slipping ratchet coupling.

adaptation.apparatus: Scale and principle teaching adaptation, not a literal book reproduction.
adaptation.scale: 0.5 mm per turn; 50 divisions per turn; nominal 0.01 mm per division. No accuracy or tolerance certification.
adaptation.specimen: Rigid 3.26 mm rod, externally inserted. Board is a teaching fixture.
adaptation.ratchet: Simplified spring-loaded axial toothed coupling. Force-limiting contact aid, not perfect constant force or calibration.
adaptation.readout: Calculated teaching overlay, no electronic sensor.
adaptation.visuals: Enlarged geometry, thread details and coupling teeth; slowed motion.
